# Kailash tool set

The page has three provenance streams. The **CLASSIC** layer follows the Kali heritage catalog, re-derived for a software-only scope. **DEFENCE** and **OPS** use the nixpkgs staple set: reproducible infrastructure, not curated exotica. **ATTACK** and the specialised edges of every layer use upstream research tooling: garak, PyRIT, promptfoo, ART, counterfit. nvfetcher pins these tools commit-exact. A pin moves only with an upstream commit.

The selection criterion is fit to the four pillars: **AppSec**, **APISec**, **MLSec**, **AISec**. **AppSec** is classic software assessment. **APISec** is web/API/AI-endpoint runtime assessment. **MLSec** is adversarial ML against predictive models. **AISec** is LLM, agentic, and MCP security. Every tool lands in exactly one primary category. A dual-use tool carries `secondary_categories` cross-refs. Duplicate rows never render.

The §3.7 no-resurrection guard holds. The distribution excludes hardware/RF/wifi/bluetooth tooling (one opt-in exception: the c-07 SDR data-pack). It also excludes paid-licence tools, cloud-only SaaS, unmaintained tools, and classic-network attack tooling (lateral movement, C2 frameworks, social engineering). The last group is Kali's network-arsenal territory. It is not the four pillars.

The census holds 32 taxonomy rows: 31 categories + 1 opt-in data-pack (`c-07-signal-sdr`). Tool rows: 270 — CLASSIC 140, ATTACK 23, OPS 82, DEFENCE 25. The §3.6 census projected ~337 primary slots. The rows fill 264 of them. Each section heading shows its open planned slots.

Generated — never hand-maintained. `python3 tools/generate-tools-page.py` fetches `tools.yaml` + `categories.yaml` from kailash-packages. The script renders every number, table, and link at generation time. A manifest merge regenerates this page.

## Field meanings

Every field a tool row can carry, in manifest order. The *In* column shows the live count of the 270 tool rows carrying the field at this revision. A smaller count marks an optional field. A row shows the field only when the row carries it.

| Field | In | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | 270/270 | Unique slug — the row's key on every generated surface (menu, CLI, modules, docs, derivations). |
| `layer` | 270/270 | `CLASSIC` · `ATTACK` · `DEFENCE` · `OPS` (the platform layer, formerly BUILD — [kailash-os#121](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/121)). All four ride a CORE substrate with no tool categories. |
| `category` | 270/270 | Primary category id — exactly one per row (the one-tool-one-primary invariant). The id orders the 31 sections on this page. |
| `secondary_categories` | 16/270 | Optional cross-refs where dual-use is real — never a second primary. The tables show it as the *also* line. |
| `name` | 270/270 | Human name (menu/docs surface). It equals `id` on all rows but one. |
| `description` | 270/270 | One line: what the tool does. The manifest holds the text. The tables truncate it. |
| `source` | 258/270 | Upstream coordinates `{vcs_owner, repo, vcs_url}`. Research-grade tools pin commit-exact (nvfetcher, `_sources/`). The field is absent on 12 rows with no declared upstream URL. Those rows render unlinked. |
| `license` | 270/270 | SPDX identifier (`GPL-2.0-only`, `MIT`, …). |
| `packaging` | 270/270 | `status` (vocabulary below) + `derivation` path on bespoke rows (71). |
| `safety` | 270/270 | `level` (vocabulary below) + `target-required` bool. The pair is inert without a declared target. The OS-side double gate reads the pair. |
| `nixos_menu` | 270/270 | Desktop-menu surface `{icon, exec, category}`. |
| `docs` | 270/270 | Generated docs path: `layers/<category>/<tool>.md`. |
| `tags` | 270/270 | Lowercase list: shape/stage markers + the `update:*` cadence class (below). |
| `atlas_tactics` | 23/270 | ≥1 MITRE ATLAS tactic id (`AML.T…`, 2026.05 matrix) — ATTACK rows only. |
| `owasp_llm` | 23/270 | Dual-epoch OWASP LLM Top 10 map `{2026: […], v2: […]}` — ATTACK rows only. The epochs stay separate and never mix (§2.4). |

### `packaging.status`

| Status | Count | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `native` | 270 | nixpkgs ships the tool. The row records the upstream coordinates that the lock builds from. |
| `stale` | 7 | nixpkgs-native. The packaged version trails upstream. The update cadence tracks the lag. No fork exists. |
| `bespoke` | 71 | Packaged in this overlay: the nvfetcher commit-exact pin, `pkgs/<tool>/default.nix`, and a committed `_sources/`. |
| `module` | 16 | Ships as a bundled module/component (service- or library-shape). It is not a single menu executable. |
| `data` | 12 | Data artefact: wordlists, corpora, pack seeds. Typically an opt-in data-pack row. |

### `safety.level`

| Level | Count | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `safe` | 255 | Runs as-is — works on artefacts, local models, or one's own systems. |
| `requires-target` | 11 | Needs a system under test as its target — authorised engagements only. |
| `exp` | 4 | Experimental research code — lab releases. The OS side double-gates it (`kailash.labMode = true` + `KAILASH_LAB_MODE=1`). |

`target-required` (9 of 270 rows, all ATTACK) — inert without a target. It renders as the `· target-required` marker in the Safety column.

### Tag update classes

The `update:*` tag on a row is the update-automation cadence class. The class sets how fast the tool's pin follows upstream. Live distribution at this revision:

| Tag | Rows |
|---|---|
| `update:slow` | 183 — The bulk cadence — steady availability, not per-commit tracking. |
| `update:steady` | 13 — Tighter tracking, not release-pinned. |
| `update:weekly` | 5 — Weekly follow — fast-moving attack tooling. |
| `update:fast` | 6 — Tightest follow — pinned-reference tools stay near upstream head. |

## C-7 · Signal &amp; SDR Processing (`c-07-signal-sdr`, CLASSIC data-pack, 6 tools)

**Purpose:** Software-only signal processing pack for ML signal work (audio/waveform corpora) and the B-6 voice-clone research surface.

*Coverage:* Medium

**Opt-in data-pack.** This category ships as the opt-in data-pack `kailash-data.sdr-tools`. Its tools stay absent from default profiles and ISOs by design. The module stub exists. It stays off on every default surface. Manifest note: the sole radio-adjacent concession (§4.1); category of record but opt-in data-pack — never on default profiles/ISOs (D7). Module stub exists but off everywhere by default; decision + revisit condition recorded in the module comment (KA-07.2).
